The Apple Goes Mushy Part I: OS X's Interface Decline (Introduction)

Not a bad article.

The problem is that OSX won't allow you to theme it. Sure having 1 GUI is nice for developers but you are stuck with what Apple gives you.

Back in Beta OSX days I loved the fresh look and so did the web. People were tired of Windows influenced themes. XP had its hay day too. Then Android and flat design came along and the shift was obvious to come and now we have material design based sites. What's next? Who knows but it won't be flat.

As for Apple, the design ethos of Jobs is legend and I too agree that you should "sand the bottom" of drawers. Too bad that Apple has probably peaked for design and since Ive's busy hob bobbing with the Queen in his Silver Cloud he won't be the one to lead the next new trend. Copying Braun older design influences has been played out.

So ... What is next???

Some things in the article I can agree with:

  • colors are good and should be used freely. There's are b/w option in accessibility and color profiles for people who prefer less color.

  • icons should be descriptive and/or intuitive. Nothing against establishing a brand with a new (at that point more or less abstract) logo, or simplification of a given logo. But someone who hasn't used a Mac before but knows other computers or basic concepts should quickly find their way. And a user after an upgrade shouldn't have to choose between 10 similar-looking abstract symbols for completely different functions.

But I disagree on skeuomorphism. That had to go. Not only was it 'lying' by fakng appearances (of function, of 3d, and others), like the cheap toys in dollar stores mimicking real stuff. It was also cluttered, and for any taste, there was one icon which was unbelievably ugly - like for me the "brown leather" address book. And it was difficult to get rid of that.

When I had my first Mac, with it's sleek silver-black appearance, starting it up felt like finding my grandpa's bureau inside. The only good looking desktops imo were the ones where the dock was reduced to 3 or 4 symbols (not too big), and icons and Launchpad were avoided.

Keeping themes where people could go back to old icons would have been a bad idea, as that would have meant having to support two different design-philosophies - even 3rd-party developers would be drowning in complaints if they only provided a more or less "flat" icon for their app - or the other way around, if they stick to skeuomorphic.

Imo better than making everything flat and abstract, would have been to turn the whole desktop 3d. With a few designs for the different apps, so people can customise lighter or darker themes, more sleek or more playful themes, more saturated or more pastel/grey/black/blue/... colors. It would even have allowed to keep some skeuomorphism as alternative skins for the different apps, at least for a while.

Besides a search, a standard menu in one of the corners, from which anything can be selected and highlighted by standard names, would help tech support and people with impairments navigate quickly.

Even the slowest Mac from 3 years ago can do 3d graphics on a browser - in the desktop, it would be much faster.
